title: SailPoint Admin Domain 6 questions (6.1, 6.2)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: An access request for an access profile has received every required approval. What happens next?
choices: The access is provisioned to the user's account on the source
The request returns to the requester to confirm it
The owner must re-aggregate the source first
A certification campaign is started for the user
questions.answer: The access is provisioned to the user's account on the source
questions.explanation: After all approvals, the tenant provisions the access, either directly through the connector or through a manual task. Certifications and aggregation are not part of the request flow.

questions.stem: An admin wants users to request a newly built access profile. Which configuration must be done FIRST?
choices: Grant every requester the Source Admin user level
Turn on Allow Access Requests for the access profile
Create a certification campaign for the access profile
Add the access profile to a lifecycle state
questions.answer: Turn on Allow Access Requests for the access profile
questions.explanation: An access item must be set up for requests before it appears in the Request Center; then the review process and comment rules are configured. Lifecycle states grant access without requests.

questions.stem: A user with two accounts on the same source requests an access profile from that source. What happens during the request?
choices: The access is added to both accounts automatically after approval
The request fails until one account is deleted
The requester selects which account should receive the access
The source owner picks the account after approval
questions.answer: The requester selects which account should receive the access
questions.explanation: When the identity has multiple accounts on a source, the requester chooses the target account for the access.

questions.stem: A request contains three access items, and the approver denies one of them. What happens to the other two?
choices: They wait until the denied item is resubmitted and approved
They are converted into a single role request
They are all canceled with the denied item
They continue through their own review and provisioning
questions.answer: They continue through their own review and provisioning
questions.explanation: Items in a request can be provisioned or canceled individually without affecting the other items.

questions.stem: An auditor wants a list of all access requests submitted last month with their status. Where should the admin get it?
choices: Search, using the Access Request Activity report
The virtual appliance health dashboard
The source's aggregation history page
The identity profile's preview page
questions.answer: Search, using the Access Request Activity report
questions.explanation: Access requests are tracked in Search through the Access Request Activity report or a query for ACCESS_REQUEST events. Aggregation and VA pages do not record requests.

questions.stem: Contractors may request a privileged access profile but must never hold it for more than 30 days. What should the admin configure on the access profile?
choices: A timeout of 30 days for pending approvals
Require End Date with a maximum duration of 30 days
A reminder every 30 days to the access profile owner
A certification campaign that runs every 30 days
questions.answer: Require End Date with a maximum duration of 30 days
questions.explanation: Require End Date with a maximum duration limits how long requested access lasts. Timeout only controls how long a pending request waits for review.

questions.stem: A user requests a role that would place them in violation of a separation of duties policy. What does the reviewer see?
choices: An error, because SoD violations block all requests
A prompt to delete the conflicting role first
A notice that granting the request would cause an SoD violation
Nothing, because SoD policies are checked only during certifications
questions.answer: A notice that granting the request would cause an SoD violation
questions.explanation: With SoD policies configured, reviewers are notified when granting a request would create a violation, and requesters see the notice too. The reviewer then decides with that information.

questions.stem: Requests for a payroll access profile must be approved by the requested-for user's manager and then by the payroll security team. What should the admin configure?
choices: Manager only, with the team added to the request as watchers
Primary Owner only, with the team set as the owner
Governance Group only, with all of the managers added to the group
Manager, then a Governance Group for the team, in that order
questions.answer: Manager, then a Governance Group for the team, in that order
questions.explanation: Multiple reviewers can be added and ordered so they are asked one after another. A governance group lets any one team member approve on the team's behalf.

questions.stem: A governance group of five people is a reviewer for an access profile. How many members must approve a request?
choices: Any one member of the group
All five members
A majority of three members
The group's first-listed member only
questions.answer: Any one member of the group
questions.explanation: Only one identity in a governance group needs to approve or deny on behalf of the group.

questions.stem: An admin enables requests on an access profile but leaves Require Approval unselected. What review applies to its requests?
choices: The item stays hidden until approval is set
The tenant's global approval configuration still applies
Every Admin in the tenant must approve it
No review at all, and access is granted instantly
questions.answer: The tenant's global approval configuration still applies
questions.explanation: If Require Approval is not chosen on the item, the global approval configuration still applies.

questions.stem: Pending approvals for an access profile should expire if nobody acts on them. What is the maximum timeout the admin can set?
choices: 365 days
7 days
90 days
30 days
questions.answer: 90 days
questions.explanation: The Timeout field sets how many days a request can wait before it expires, with 90 days as the maximum.

questions.stem: Reviewers must explain why they reject requests for a sensitive access profile. What should the admin configure?
choices: Require an access request form for every requester to complete
Require reauthentication for every requester
Require a maximum duration for the access profile
Require Comments when a reviewer denies the request
questions.answer: Require Comments when a reviewer denies the request
questions.explanation: Require Comments has options for when the user requests access and when a reviewer denies it. A request form collects requester input, not reviewer reasons.

questions.stem: An approval has gone through the whole escalation chain and nobody has acted. Who receives it next?
choices: The configured fallback approver
The SailPoint support team
The virtual appliance service account
The requester, to approve it themselves
questions.answer: The configured fallback approver
questions.explanation: A request goes to the fallback approver after it has passed the full escalation chain without action.

questions.stem: An admin wants a request approval to be handled by an automated workflow instead of named reviewers. Which workflows can be selected?
choices: Workflows that run on a daily schedule
Enabled workflows that use the Access Request Submitted trigger
Any workflow, whether enabled or disabled
Any workflow that uses the Identity Created trigger, enabled or not
questions.answer: Enabled workflows that use the Access Request Submitted trigger
questions.explanation: The Workflow review option lists only enabled workflows that use the Access Request Submitted trigger.

questions.stem: A role contains an access profile that requires source owner approval. A user requests the role. Which approval process applies?
choices: Both the role and the access profile processes
The access profile's approval process only
The role's own approval process
No approval, because roles bypass reviews
questions.answer: The role's own approval process
questions.explanation: Requests for a role use the role's approval process; an access profile's process applies only to requests for that access profile itself.

questions.stem: A request has three reviewers in order: manager, owner and governance group. The owner denies it. What happens?
choices: The request returns to the manager for a final decision
The access is provisioned with a warning
The governance group can still approve it
The review stops and the access is not provisioned
questions.answer: The review stops and the access is not provisioned
questions.explanation: Reviewers are asked in the configured order, all must approve, and a denial stops the review so nothing is provisioned.

questions.stem: The owner of an access profile requests it for themselves, and they are its only configured reviewer. What happens by default?
choices: The approval is reassigned to the requester's manager
The request waits until the access profile owner is changed
The request is approved automatically
The request is denied as a self-approval
questions.answer: The approval is reassigned to the requester's manager
questions.explanation: Self-approval is prevented by default: when the requester or recipient is the reviewer, the individual approval goes to their manager. Auto-approval for this case is only available through API configuration.

questions.stem: A requester belongs to the governance group that reviews the access they requested. How does self-approval prevention handle this?
choices: The group is skipped and the request auto-approved
The requester is omitted, and other group members review it
The requester is allowed to approve as a group member
The request is canceled and must be resubmitted
questions.answer: The requester is omitted, and other group members review it
questions.explanation: For governance group reviews, the requester and recipient are left out of the review. If they are the only member, it goes to their manager instead.

questions.stem: One reviewer configured for an access item cannot be resolved, for example because the identity no longer exists. Who is tried FIRST?
choices: The requested access item's owner
A random org admin
The missing reviewer's manager
The fallback approver
questions.answer: The missing reviewer's manager
questions.explanation: For a missing reviewer, the tenant tries the reviewer's manager, then the escalation chain, the fallback approver, the item owner and finally an org admin.

questions.stem: A manager receives an email about a pending access request. Where in Identity Security Cloud does the manager act on it?
choices: In Admin > Identity Management > Identity Profiles
In Admin > Access Model > Roles
On the Request Center's Access Items tab
On the Approvals page
questions.answer: On the Approvals page
questions.explanation: Every user, including those with no admin level, has an Approvals page for reviews assigned to them. Admin pages are not needed to approve.

questions.stem: Approvals for a high-risk entitlement must confirm the reviewer is really present when they approve. What should the admin enable?
choices: Reauthenticated approvals for the item
A longer request timeout
Escalations to the fallback approver after one day
A maximum duration for the access
questions.answer: Reauthenticated approvals for the item
questions.explanation: Reauthenticated approvals require reviewers to authenticate again when approving sensitive or regulated access.

questions.stem: Escalations are enabled on an access profile, and the first reviewer has not acted after the configured number of days. What happens?
choices: The request is denied automatically and the requester is notified
The approval moves to the next approver in the escalation chain
The access profile is disabled
The request is approved automatically
questions.answer: The approval moves to the next approver in the escalation chain
questions.explanation: Escalations forward unhandled approvals along the escalation chain on the configured schedule, ending with the fallback approver. They do not approve or deny automatically.

questions.stem: A manager wants a requested access profile removed from a direct report who changed projects. What can the manager do?
choices: Change the user's lifecycle state to inactive
Delete the user's account from the source page
Submit an access removal request for the team member
Edit the access profile for everyone
questions.answer: Submit an access removal request for the team member
questions.explanation: Managers can request removal of access their direct reports obtained through requests. Editing the access profile would affect everyone who holds it.

questions.stem: What is always required when a user submits an access removal request?
choices: An approval from the source owner
An access request form
A certification decision
A comment
questions.answer: A comment
questions.explanation: Removal requests always require comments when submitted. Approval for removals is optional and off by default.

questions.stem: A manager tries to request removal of an access profile that the user received through a lifecycle state. Why is it not allowed?
choices: Access granted by a lifecycle state or role cannot be removed that way
The manager needs the Cert Admin user level
Only a certification can remove lifecycle state access
Removal requests work only for entitlements
questions.answer: Access granted by a lifecycle state or role cannot be removed that way
questions.explanation: Only access profiles that are not part of the user's assigned roles or lifecycle state can be removed through removal requests. That access is controlled by the role or lifecycle configuration.

questions.stem: An admin enables requests on an access profile but configures nothing for removals. What review do removal requests need?
choices: Approval by every additional owner
No approval, because removal approval is off by default
Manager approval, because it is always required
The same approvals as add requests
questions.answer: No approval, because removal approval is off by default
questions.explanation: By default no approvals are required for removal; Require Approval for Removal adds reviewers when needed.

questions.stem: Which roles can a manager remove from a direct report through a removal request?
choices: Any role, including those assigned by criteria
Only roles that contain a single entitlement
Requestable roles the user obtained through an access request
Only disabled roles that are still assigned
questions.answer: Requestable roles the user obtained through an access request
questions.explanation: Only roles obtained through access requests can be removed this way, so the role must be requestable. Criteria-based roles follow their assignment rules.

questions.stem: Which work items can a work reassignment configuration redirect to another user?
choices: Only aggregation schedules and source errors
Only password resets and MFA enrollments
Only certifications, and only after their campaign has been completed
Access request reviews, certifications and manual provisioning tasks
questions.answer: Access request reviews, certifications and manual provisioning tasks
questions.explanation: Work reassignment redirects access request reviews, certifications and manual provisioning tasks assigned to a user.

questions.stem: A manager will be on leave for three weeks and wants pending approvals handled by a deputy. Who can set up the reassignment?
choices: The manager, the manager's own manager or an admin
Only the owner of each access profile
Only an admin who also holds the Helpdesk user level
Only SailPoint support
questions.answer: The manager, the manager's own manager or an admin
questions.explanation: Users can define reassignments for themselves, managers for their team members and admins for anyone.

questions.stem: An admin must set up work reassignment for an identity who is unexpectedly absent. Where does the admin do this?
choices: In Admin > Global > Email Templates
The identity's Work Reassignment tab under Identity Management > Identities
On the source's Provisioning tab
In the lifecycle states of the identity profile that the identity belongs to
questions.answer: The identity's Work Reassignment tab under Identity Management > Identities
questions.explanation: Admins add reassignment configurations for any identity from the identity's Work Reassignment tab.

questions.stem: An admin wants one identity's approvals and certifications sent to a deputy. How many configurations are needed?
choices: None, because managers receive all work automatically
Three, because certifications need two entries
Two, because each configuration covers one work item type
One, because one covers every work item type
questions.answer: Two, because each configuration covers one work item type
questions.explanation: Only one work item type can be chosen per reassignment configuration, so each type needs its own.

questions.stem: User A reassigns work to User B, and User B tries to reassign work back to User A for the same period. What happens?
choices: The second reassignment replaces the first
Both users receive every work item twice
Work goes to an admin at random
The tenant prevents reassignments that create a loop
questions.answer: The tenant prevents reassignments that create a loop
questions.explanation: Identity Security Cloud blocks work reassignments that would create loops in reassignment chains.

questions.stem: A reassignment period ends. What happens to approvals that were reassigned while it was active?
choices: They stay with the user they were reassigned to
They return to the original user
They are canceled and must be resubmitted
They are escalated to the fallback approver
questions.answer: They stay with the user they were reassigned to
questions.explanation: When a reassignment ends or is deleted, items that were already reassigned remain with the new owner.

questions.stem: A user's approvals are reassigned to a deputy, but one request was submitted by that deputy. Who reviews that request?
choices: The requester's original manager, but only after a 90-day timeout
Someone other than the deputy, because self-approval is prevented
No one, and the request is approved automatically
The deputy, because reassignment overrides prevention
questions.answer: Someone other than the deputy, because self-approval is prevented
questions.explanation: In access request review reassignment, self-approval prevention stops reassignment to the requester and the access recipient.

questions.stem: A senior executive should never receive certifications or approvals, permanently. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Disable the executive's email notifications
Remove the executive's manager attribute
A work reassignment with no end date to a delegate
Give the executive the Admin user level
questions.answer: A work reassignment with no end date to a delegate
questions.explanation: Work reassignment supports permanent redirection for users who should not receive these tasks, such as senior executives or service identities.

questions.stem: Put the steps of an access request with two reviewers in order.
items: The user selects the access profile in the Request Center and adds a comment
The request is submitted and the first reviewer, the manager, is notified
The manager approves on the Approvals page
A member of the governance group approves
The access is provisioned to the user's source account
questions.explanation: Reviewers are asked in the configured order and all must approve before provisioning. A denial at any step would stop the request.

questions.stem: Match each reviewer option to who approves the request.

pairs.match: The manager of the identity receiving the access
The identity configured to own the access item
Any one member of the selected group
Any one of the item's secondary owners

targets_extra: Every member of the selected group in turn
questions.explanation: Reviewer options decide who is asked. For a governance group or additional owners, one member's decision is enough; nobody approves in turn on the group's behalf.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about work reassignment in Identity Security Cloud are correct?
choices: Managers can add reassignments for their team members
Items already reassigned stay with the new owner after the period ends
One configuration can cover every work item type at once
Reassignment chains that loop back are allowed
Only SailPoint support can create reassignments
answers: Managers can add reassignments for their team members
Items already reassigned stay with the new owner after the period ends
questions.explanation: Users, their managers and admins can create reassignments, and reassigned items stay with the new owner. Each configuration covers one work type and loops are blocked.

questions.stem: An admin selects Preview Campaign for a new manager campaign. What should happen before reviewers receive any work?
choices: Reviewers approve the preview before it starts
The campaign starts once the preview is ready
SailPoint support activates the campaign
The admin reviews the preview and then selects Start Campaign
questions.answer: The admin reviews the preview and then selects Start Campaign
questions.explanation: A campaign is created, previewed and then started by the admin; reviewers get their certifications only after Start Campaign.

questions.stem: A campaign preview was generated four days ago but never started. What does SailPoint recommend?
choices: Delete it and create the campaign again
Extend the deadline and start it
Reassign all reviewers, then start it
Start it, because previews never go stale
questions.answer: Delete it and create the campaign again
questions.explanation: Campaigns should be started within a day of generating the preview; otherwise they should be deleted and recreated so the data is current.

questions.stem: An admin creates a campaign and does not change the deadline field. When is it due?
choices: At the end of the calendar quarter
Two weeks after the creation date
One week after the creation date
Thirty days after the start date
questions.answer: Two weeks after the creation date
questions.explanation: The default deadline for a certification campaign is two weeks after the creation date.

questions.stem: A new campaign's filter removes every entitlement, so the campaign has no content. What does the admin see?
choices: A preview that lists every identity in the tenant with no access items
An active campaign with no reviewers
No preview, and the campaign appears empty in the Completed tab
A reviewer certification asking for a filter
questions.answer: No preview, and the campaign appears empty in the Completed tab
questions.explanation: If a campaign contains no identities or access items, no preview is created and it appears as an empty campaign in the Completed tab.

questions.stem: An admin returns to a previewed campaign after its due date to start it. What happens?
choices: The campaign starts and completes immediately
The campaign starts but sends no emails
The campaign starts and its deadline is moved forward automatically
The campaign cannot be started once its due date has passed
questions.answer: The campaign cannot be started once its due date has passed
questions.explanation: A previewed campaign can be started later, but not after its due date has passed.

questions.stem: Email notifications were left enabled for a campaign. When do reviewers receive reminder emails by default?
choices: When the campaign is activated and every seven days until they sign off
Only after the admin selects Email for each reviewer on the campaign card
Only on the deadline date
Every day from activation to completion
questions.answer: When the campaign is activated and every seven days until they sign off
questions.explanation: Certification emails go out at activation and then every seven days until the reviewer signs off, the certification expires or the campaign is completed. Admins can also email reviewers manually.

questions.stem: A manager was assigned to a team after a manager campaign was generated. Why does the new manager not see the team's certification?
choices: Managers must be Cert Admins to see certifications
Campaigns are generated as a snapshot in time
The campaign shows only identities with no manager
Reviewer changes need a configuration hub restore
questions.answer: Campaigns are generated as a snapshot in time
questions.explanation: Campaigns capture data when they are generated, so later manager changes are not reflected. The certification can be reassigned if needed.

questions.stem: All reviewers in a campaign signed off before the deadline. What must the admin do to finish the campaign?
choices: Run an aggregation on every source in the campaign
Delete the campaign so it stops sending emails
Nothing, because the campaign moves to Completed automatically
Select Complete and choose whether to revoke the undecided items
questions.answer: Nothing, because the campaign moves to Completed automatically
questions.explanation: When every reviewer has made decisions and signed off, the campaign completes automatically with no admin action for approvals.

questions.stem: Each manager must review the access of their direct reports once a year. Which campaign type fits BEST?
choices: Search campaign of uncorrelated accounts
Source owner campaign
Role composition campaign
Manager campaign
questions.answer: Manager campaign
questions.explanation: Manager campaigns send each manager a certification of their direct reports' access. Source owner campaigns are organised by source instead.

questions.stem: A tightly controlled trading system has few licences, and its owner must review everyone with access to it. Which campaign type fits BEST?
choices: Source owner campaign for that source
Manager campaign for the whole tenant
Role composition campaign for all roles
Manager campaign filtered to executives
questions.answer: Source owner campaign for that source
questions.explanation: Source owner campaigns let owners review access only on the sources they own and suit limited-licence or restricted systems.

questions.stem: A source owner campaign for three sources does not generate certifications for one of them. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: That source's accounts are all correlated
That source has no source owner assigned
That source has requestable entitlements
That source uses a virtual appliance
questions.answer: That source has no source owner assigned
questions.explanation: Source owner campaigns generate only for sources with an assigned source owner, so the owner must be set on the source first.

questions.stem: Role owners must confirm that each role still contains the right access profiles and entitlements. Which campaign should the admin create?
choices: A campaign of uncorrelated accounts
A manager campaign
A role composition campaign
A source owner campaign
questions.answer: A role composition campaign
questions.explanation: Role composition campaigns review what a role contains rather than who holds it.

questions.stem: Some identities have no manager, and the admin wants them included in a review with manager as the reviewer. What should the admin do?
choices: Run a standard manager campaign, which already includes those identities
Run a role composition campaign for their roles
Set each identity as its own manager first
Create the campaign from Search and choose Manager as the reviewer
questions.answer: Create the campaign from Search and choose Manager as the reviewer
questions.explanation: Standard manager campaigns exclude identities without managers. Campaigns created from Search with Manager as reviewer include them, sending them to the campaign owner.

questions.stem: Security wants everyone who holds three privileged database entitlements reviewed, across all departments. Which approach fits BEST?
choices: A campaign created from Search that targets those access items
A role composition campaign for every role that contains database access
A source owner campaign for every source
A manager campaign for every department
questions.answer: A campaign created from Search that targets those access items
questions.explanation: Search-based campaigns can target specific identities or access items found by a query. A manager campaign would review all access of all reports.

questions.stem: An admin wants a manager campaign that covers only entitlements from finance systems. What should the admin apply?
choices: A governance group
A campaign filter
A segment
A lifecycle state
questions.answer: A campaign filter
questions.explanation: Campaign filters limit certifications to a subset of entitlements or users. Segments control requestable access visibility.

questions.stem: Which certifications can an admin create from Search in Identity Security Cloud?
choices: Only certifications of uncorrelated accounts
Only manager certifications for one department
Certifications of identities, access items and role compositions
Only source owner certifications, and only for flat file sources
questions.answer: Certifications of identities, access items and role compositions
questions.explanation: Starting a campaign from Search supports certifying identities, access items and role compositions.

questions.stem: A reviewer marked several items Revoke but closed the certification without signing off. What happens to those decisions?
choices: They are converted to approvals
They are sent to the original requester of each item for approval
They are applied immediately
They are not applied until the reviewer signs off
questions.answer: They are not applied until the reviewer signs off
questions.explanation: Revoke decisions that are not signed off are not applied; sign-off triggers remediation.

questions.stem: A reviewer goes on leave mid-campaign and has not signed off. What can the admin do?
choices: Reassign the certification to another reviewer
Change the campaign type to source owner and restart it
Copy the reviewer's password to a deputy
Delete the reviewer's identity
questions.answer: Reassign the certification to another reviewer
questions.explanation: Admins can reassign certifications of reviewers who have not yet signed off. A certification that is already signed off cannot be reassigned.

questions.stem: A manager's certification includes the manager's own access. How does Identity Security Cloud handle this?
choices: It lets the manager approve it with a comment
It moves that access to a separate certification for another reviewer
It removes the manager's own access from the campaign entirely and silently
It revokes the access automatically
questions.answer: It moves that access to a separate certification for another reviewer
questions.explanation: Self-certification is prevented by moving the access to another certification, sent to the identity's manager, else the campaign owner, else a random admin.

questions.stem: An admin tries to manually reassign a certification to a new reviewer, but the reassignment is blocked. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The campaign deadline is more than a week away
The certification contains fewer than ten identities to review
The certification contains the new reviewer's own access
The new reviewer is not a Cert Admin
questions.answer: The certification contains the new reviewer's own access
questions.explanation: Manual reassignment is blocked when the certification includes access belonging to the new owner, preventing self-review.

questions.stem: Which two decisions does a reviewer make on access items that were obtained through access requests?
choices: Enable or Disable
Escalate or Delegate
Aggregate or Correlate
Approve or Revoke
questions.answer: Approve or Revoke
questions.explanation: Reviewers approve access that should stay and revoke access that should be removed. Aggregation and correlation are source operations.

questions.stem: Auditors want reviewers to justify every revoke decision in a campaign. Where should the admin configure this?
choices: In the campaign's settings for when reviewers must leave comments
In the global access request approval settings for the whole tenant
In each source's account schema
In each reviewer's work reassignment
questions.answer: In the campaign's settings for when reviewers must leave comments
questions.explanation: When creating a campaign, the admin chooses when reviewers are required to leave comments on their decisions.

questions.stem: Which identity details appear to reviewers in certifications by default to help them decide?
choices: Employee ID, salary and home address
Email, lifecycle state and manager
Account IDs on every connected source
Password, MFA method and last sign-in
questions.answer: Email, lifecycle state and manager
questions.explanation: Certifications show email, lifecycle state and manager by default, and up to five more attributes can be added through the public identity configuration API.

questions.stem: A role assigned to identities by membership criteria appears in a certification. What can the reviewer do with it?
choices: Convert it into a requested role
Revoke it, which removes it permanently
Only acknowledge it, because the role model controls the assignment
Delete the role from the tenant
questions.answer: Only acknowledge it, because the role model controls the assignment
questions.explanation: Roles assigned by criteria can only be acknowledged in certifications, because criteria are evaluated daily and would add the identity back.

questions.stem: A reviewer wants to revoke a criteria-assigned role from one identity. What will actually remove it?
choices: Revoking it twice in two campaigns
Asking the source owner to delete the account
Disabling email notifications for the campaign
Changing the role's criteria or the identity's data so it no longer matches
questions.answer: Changing the role's criteria or the identity's data so it no longer matches
questions.explanation: Auto-assigned roles follow their criteria, so the criteria or the identity's attributes must change for the role to be removed.

questions.stem: Access profiles granted by the identity's lifecycle state do not appear in a manager campaign. Why?
choices: Lifecycle state access profiles are not included in certifications
They appear only in role composition campaigns
They appear only after the lifecycle state changes
A default campaign filter hides them
questions.answer: Lifecycle state access profiles are not included in certifications
questions.explanation: Access profiles from the assigned lifecycle state do not appear in certifications at all; they are governed by the lifecycle configuration.

questions.stem: An identity holds an access profile through a role. How does this access appear in a certification?
choices: It does not appear and cannot be reviewed
Within the role, and it can be managed only through that role
As a separate access profile item that the reviewer can revoke on its own
As individual entitlements for each source
questions.answer: Within the role, and it can be managed only through that role
questions.explanation: Access profiles granted through a role are encapsulated in the role and can only be managed through it.

questions.stem: When does an entitlement appear as its own item in a certification?
choices: Only when it is marked requestable
Only when it is marked privileged
When it is not encapsulated in one of the user's access profiles or roles
Only when it came from a flat file source
questions.answer: When it is not encapsulated in one of the user's access profiles or roles
questions.explanation: Entitlements can be certified individually only if they are not part of the user's access profiles or roles.

questions.stem: A user's entitlements exactly match an access profile they never requested. How is that access shown in a manager certification?
choices: Not at all, because it was not requested
As an uncorrelated account
As individual entitlements, because it was not requested
As the access profile, not as individual entitlements
questions.answer: As the access profile, not as individual entitlements
questions.explanation: When an identity's entitlements match an access profile, the identity is granted that access profile and the entitlements are certified as that access profile.

questions.stem: A reviewer revokes an entitlement on a direct-connected source that supports provisioning and signs off. How is the access removed?
choices: Automatically, through the source connector
By the reviewer editing the source
By a manual task that is created for the source owner
At the next certification campaign
questions.answer: Automatically, through the source connector
questions.explanation: With a direct connection that can provision, remediation is automatic after sign-off.

questions.stem: Access is revoked on a source that the tenant cannot write to. How is the revocation carried out?
choices: The revocation is discarded without notice
A task is created for the source owner to remove the access manually
The identity is disabled across every source included in the campaign
The source is automatically deleted
questions.answer: A task is created for the source owner to remove the access manually
questions.explanation: When the tenant cannot provision to a source, manual remediation creates a task for the source owner to make the change.

questions.stem: After a campaign, the admin needs to confirm that revoked items on non-connected sources were actually removed. What should the admin use?
choices: The virtual appliance health report
The aggregation history of the authoritative source
The Campaign Remediation Status Report
The Identities Without Managers report
questions.answer: The Campaign Remediation Status Report
questions.explanation: The Campaign Remediation Status Report shows revoked items that could not be deprovisioned automatically; regenerate it to confirm removal.

questions.stem: A campaign uses the default setting for undecided items, and the admin completes it after the deadline. What happens to undecided items?
choices: They are sent to the source owners
Access is revoked for all of them once the admin completes it
They move to the next campaign
Access is maintained, because they are treated as approved
questions.answer: Access is maintained, because they are treated as approved
questions.explanation: Maintaining access to undecided items is the default; such items are approved when the admin completes the campaign.

questions.stem: When creating a campaign, an admin can choose 'choose to maintain or revoke access to undecided items'. Why does SailPoint recommend maintaining access instead?
choices: Reinstating access after it is revoked is difficult
Revoking undecided items is not technically possible
Maintaining access deletes the campaign history
Revoking requires a separate SailPoint licence
questions.answer: Reinstating access after it is revoked is difficult
questions.explanation: Bulk revocation of undecided items can remove access people still need, and restoring it is hard. That is why maintaining access is the recommended option.

questions.stem: Where can an admin confirm that access revoked on direct-connected sources was removed after a campaign?
choices: Admin > Access Model > Segments
Admin > Identity Management > Activities
Admin > Connections > Virtual Appliances
Admin > Global > Email Templates
questions.answer: Admin > Identity Management > Activities
questions.explanation: Activities shows provisioning activity, including access revoked automatically because of a certification.

questions.stem: An admin deletes an active campaign by mistake. What is the result for reviewers?
choices: All revoke decisions are applied before deletion
Reviewers keep their decisions and receive a warning email from the tenant
Decisions are lost and the certifications vanish without any notification
The campaign is restored automatically after 24 hours
questions.answer: Decisions are lost and the certifications vanish without any notification
questions.explanation: Deleting a campaign loses any decisions made, removes the certifications from participants' views and sends no notification.

questions.stem: Put the stages of a manager certification campaign in order.
items: Create the campaign and set its name, deadline and options
Select Preview Campaign and review the preview
Select Start Campaign so reviewers are notified
Reviewers approve or revoke items and sign off
Revoked access is remediated and the campaign completes
questions.explanation: Campaigns are configured, previewed and started by the admin. Reviewer sign-off triggers remediation, and the campaign completes when all are signed off or the admin completes it.

questions.stem: Match each campaign type to what it reviews.

pairs.match: Access of each manager's direct reports
Access on the sources each owner owns
The access items each role contains
Identities or access items found by a query

targets_extra: Pending access requests in the approval queue
questions.explanation: Each type selects reviewers and content differently. Pending requests are handled through approvals, not certifications.

questions.stem: Which TWO kinds of access can a reviewer revoke in a certification?
choices: A role the user received through an access request
An access profile the user received through an access request
A role assigned by membership criteria
An access profile granted by the user's lifecycle state
An access profile granted inside a role
answers: A role the user received through an access request
An access profile the user received through an access request
questions.explanation: Requested roles and access profiles can be approved or revoked. Criteria-based roles can only be acknowledged, lifecycle access does not appear, and access inside a role is managed through the role.
